title: Stokes residual estimates, Couette stability and linear vortex-sheet modes

items.title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, meaning a bounded connected open set whose boundary is locally a $C^1$ graph and which lies on one side of that graph after a rigid change of coordinates. Let $\mu>0$, $w\in C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $q\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, and $f\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$; $C^k(\overline\Omega)$ means that derivatives through order $k$ extend continuously to the closure. For ordinary Euclidean coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, set $\partial_j=\partial/\partial x_j$, define $
abla r=(\partial_1r,\ldots,\partial_nr)$ for scalar $r$, define $
abla\cdot v=\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_i v_i$ and $(
abla v)_{ij}=\partial_jv_i$ for vector $v$, define $(v\cdot
abla)v=\sum_{j=1}^n v_j\partial_jv$, and define the vector Laplacian by $(\Delta v)_i=\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_j^2v_i$. For $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathbb R^n$ set $|a|=(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2)^{1/2}$, so $|
abla v|^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^n|\partial_jv_i|^2$. For vector fields $g,v$, write $\|g\|_2=(\int_\Omega|g|^2\,dx)^{1/2}$ and $\|
abla v\|_2=(\int_\Omega\sum_{i,j=1}^n|\partial_jv_i|^2\,dx)^{1/2}$. Suppose pointwise that $
abla\cdot w=0$, $w|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, and $-\mu\Delta w+
abla q=f$. Also assume that a stated constant $C_\Omega>0$ satisfies the zero-trace Poincare inequality $\|v\|_2\le C_\Omega\|
abla v\|_2$ for every $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$ with $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0$. Then

$$\|
abla w\|_2\le  rac{C_\Omega}{\mu}\|f\|_2,\qquad \|w\|_2\le  rac{C_\Omega^2}{\mu}\|f\|_2.$$

For $L_x,L_z,h>0$, set $\mathbb T_L=\mathbb R/(L\mathbb Z)$ for $L>0$ and $Q=\mathbb T_{L_x}	imes(0,h)	imes\mathbb T_{L_z}$, the periodic channel cell. A field on $\overline Q$ is identified with its lift to $\mathbb R	imes[0,h]	imes\mathbb R$ periodic with periods $L_x,L_z$ in the first and third coordinates. Integrals on $Q$ use Lebesgue measure on one fundamental cell in each periodic coordinate; $\|v\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=\int_Q|v|^2$ and $\|
abla v\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=\int_Q\sum_{i,j=1}^3|\partial_jv_i|^2$. Every $v\in C^1(\overline Q;\mathbb R^3)$ periodic in the two torus variables and zero on $y=0,h$ satisfies $\|v\|_{L^2(Q)}\le h\|
abla v\|_{L^2(Q)}$. This channel inequality is a separate direct estimate on the periodic cell; it does not treat that cell as a bounded $C^1$ Euclidean domain.

In dimension three, let $ho_0>0$, $
u=\mu/ho_0$, and suppose already-existing time-independent fields $u_{m NS},u_{m S}\in C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ and $p_{m NS},p_{m S}\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ are divergence-free, have the same boundary velocity, and satisfy the constant-density incompressible Navier-Stokes and Stokes equations $ho_0(u_{m NS}\cdot
abla)u_{m NS}+
abla p_{m NS}-\mu\Delta u_{m NS}=0$ and $
abla p_{m S}-\mu\Delta u_{m S}=0$. If $f=-ho_0(u_{m NS}\cdot
abla)u_{m NS}$, then the preceding estimate applies to $w=u_{m NS}-u_{m S}$ and $q=p_{m NS}-p_{m S}$ whenever the stated Poincare bound holds. This is an a-posteriori residual estimate for already-given fields; it asserts no solution existence, no exterior-domain bound, and no error bound from Reynolds number alone. The constant $C_\Omega=h$ established for the periodic channel is not transferred to an exterior domain.

items.scope: Given smooth Stokes-difference fields, zero trace and an explicit Poincare bound, the residual controls the L2 velocity and gradient; the periodic channel has the direct bound C=h. The result asserts no solution existence, exterior-domain estimate, or Reynolds-number-only error. The bounded-domain divergence step assumes AC_omega.

items.scope: Existing smooth incompressible Navier-Stokes perturbation periodic in x,z and zero trace at y=0,h; energy decays if |S|h^2/nu<2 on its assumed smooth existence interval. This is a sufficient, nonsharp bound, not global three-dimensional regularity or a transition threshold; the planned dependency closure carries AC_omega.

items.title: Linear vortex-sheet growing modes
items.statement:
For $x,t\in\mathbb R$, assume the fields are independent of a third spatial coordinate. Let $H_+=[0,\infty)$ and $H_-=(-\infty,0]$. The real-valued interface displacement is a $C^\infty$ map $\eta:\mathbb R_x\times\mathbb R_t\to\mathbb R$, and the real-valued scalar potentials are maps $\phi_\pm:\mathbb R_x\times H_\pm\times\mathbb R_t\to\mathbb R$. Each $\phi_\pm$ is $C^\infty$ on the open half-domain; $\phi_\pm$ and their first partial derivatives $\partial_x\phi_\pm$, $\partial_y\phi_\pm$, and $\partial_t\phi_\pm$ admit continuous one-sided traces at $y=0$, locally in $(x,t)$. On the open half-domains use ordinary pointwise Euclidean derivatives in $(x,y)$ and set $\Delta=\partial_{xx}+\partial_{yy}$. Let $U_+,U_-\in\mathbb R$ be constant horizontal base velocities, and let the two half-planes $y>0$ and $y<0$ have the same constant density $\rho_0>0$. The potentials satisfy $\Delta\phi_\pm=0$ and, for every fixed $(x,t)$, $\phi_\pm$, $\partial_x\phi_\pm$, $\partial_y\phi_\pm$, and $\partial_t\phi_\pm$ tend to zero as $y\to+\infty$ and $y\to-\infty$ respectively. The stipulated linear interface equations, interpreted by one-sided traces at $y=0$, are $(\partial_t+U_\pm\partial_x)\eta=\partial_y\phi_\pm$ and continuity of the defined pressure perturbations $p'_\pm(x,t)=-\rho_0[\partial_t\phi_\pm+U_\pm\partial_x\phi_\pm]_{y=0^\pm}$. Gravity and surface tension are absent. Complexify this real linear system for the following normal-mode calculation.

For every real $k>0$, every nonzero complex amplitude $H$, and every $A_+,A_-,\lambda\in\mathbb C$, consider a mode of the form $\eta=H e^{ikx+\lambda t}$, $\phi_+=A_+e^{-ky}e^{ikx+\lambda t}$, $\phi_-=A_-e^{ky}e^{ikx+\lambda t}$. Set $\overline U=(U_++U_-)/2$ and $\Delta U=U_+-U_-$. The mode equations require

$$\lambda=-ik\overline U\pm \frac{k|\Delta U|}{2}.$$

If $\Delta U\ne0$, one root has positive real part $k|\Delta U|/2$, and its real or imaginary part gives a real exponentially growing solution of the stated linear system.

For the $2\pi$-periodic interface, require the fields to be periodic in $x$ and set $\mathbb T_{2\pi}=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. For a complex-valued trigonometric polynomial $\eta$ on this torus, define $\widehat\eta_j=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}\eta(x)e^{-ijx}\,dx$ and, for $m\ge0$, $\|\eta\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}(1+j^2)^m|\widehat\eta_j|^2$. Let $H^m(\mathbb T_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$ be the completion of the complex-valued trigonometric polynomials in this norm; real-valued fields are viewed as elements of its real subspace. If $\Delta U\ne0$, then for every fixed $t>0$ this exact mode family has bounded initial $H^m$ norm but unbounded evolved $H^m$ norm as its integer wavenumber $k\to\infty$. Thus no uniform estimate of the form $\|\eta(t)\|_{H^m}\le C_t\|\eta(0)\|_{H^m}$ holds for this family. This is a linear interface-model conclusion, not a theorem of nonlinear turbulent transition, viscous shear-layer behavior, or physical instability in a particular experiment.

title: Stokes residual estimates, Couette stability and linear vortex-sheet modes — Examples

items.title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate — formal worked field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $L_x,L_z,h,\mu>0$, define $\mathbb T_L=\mathbb R/(L\mathbb Z)$ for $L>0$, and set $Q=\mathbb T_{L_x}	imes(0,h)	imes\mathbb T_{L_z}$. Regard fields on $Q$ as periodic lifts to $\mathbb R	imes(0,h)	imes\mathbb R$ with periods $L_x,L_z$ in $x,z$, and integrate with Lebesgue measure over one fundamental cell in each periodic coordinate. Set $w(x,y,z)=(\sin(\pi y/h),0,0)$, $q=0$, and $f=\mu(\pi/h)^2w$. Then $w$ is a smooth divergence-free periodic field with zero trace on both $y$ walls and satisfies $-\mu\Delta w+
abla q=f$. Its norms satisfy $\|w\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=L_xL_z h/2$ and $\|
abla w\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=(\pi/h)^2\|w\|_{L^2(Q)}^2$, so $\|w\|_{L^2(Q)}=(h/\pi)\|
abla w\|_{L^2(Q)}\le h\|
abla w\|_{L^2(Q)}$. This is a formal worked field for the periodic-channel Poincare clause; the general bounded $C^1$ Euclidean residual theorem is not applied to this periodic cell.
items.scope: Explicit smooth periodic-channel residual field with zero trace, the valid nonsharp channel Poincare bound C=h, and this field's exact norm ratio h/pi. It verifies that channel clause only; it does not apply the bounded C1 Euclidean residual estimate to the periodic quotient cell.

items.title: Conditional nonlinear Couette energy stability — formal worked field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Define $\mathbb T_{2\pi}=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and let $Q=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times(0,1)\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$, with Lebesgue integration over one fundamental cell. Take $\rho_0=\mu=\nu=1$, $S=1$, base field $U_b=(y,0,0)$, and pressure $p=0$. For any $a\in\mathbb R$, set
$$u(x,y,z,t)=(y+a e^{-\pi^2t}\sin(\pi y),0,0),\qquad t\ge0.$$
This field is smooth, periodic in $x,z$, divergence-free, and has wall values $0$ at $y=0$ and $(1,0,0)$ at $y=1$. Its perturbation $w=u-U_b$ satisfies $\|w(t)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=e^{-2\pi^2t}\|w(0)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2\le e^{-t}\|w(0)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2$. The sufficient parameter condition in the supplier is $|S|h^2/\nu=1<2$; this example verifies that conditional bound for one exact field.
items.scope: The exact smooth Couette perturbation field on a unit-height periodic channel; verifies the sufficient energy bound at |S|h^2/nu=1. It adds no general existence or transition claim and inherits the supplier's AC_omega qualification.

items.title: Linear vortex-sheet growing modes — worked interpretation
items.statement:
On the periodic interface $x\in\mathbb T_{2\pi}$, where $\mathbb T_{2\pi}=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, with half-planes $y>0$ and $y<0$, take equal density $\rho_0=1$, base velocities $U_+=1$ and $U_-=-1$, and no gravity or surface tension. For $t\ge0$, define
$$\eta(x,t)=e^t\cos x,\qquad \phi_+(x,y,t)=e^{t-y}(\sin x-\cos x),\qquad \phi_-(x,y,t)=e^{t+y}(\cos x+\sin x).$$
The potentials are harmonic and decay at their respective infinities; at $y=0$ they satisfy $(\partial_t+U_\pm\partial_x)\eta=\partial_y\phi_\pm$ and continuity of $p'_\pm=-(\partial_t+U_\pm\partial_x)\phi_\pm$. Thus these fields give an exact real growing mode of the stipulated linear interface equations.
items.scope: Equal-density, no-gravity/no-surface-tension linear interface model with U+=1, U_-=-1, and k=1. It verifies one exact real growing mode and makes no nonlinear transition or experimental claim.
